findings.observation: Searched the entire project directory for patterns indicating new roadway construction ('new roadway', 'roadway construction', 'plan profile roadway'). No files matched these patterns. Reviewed README sheet index (52 sheets) — no sheets titled as roadway construction plans. Examined facts.md showing this is an infill development on existing streets (South Lamar Blvd, Collier St, Evergreen Ave, Kinney Ave). The project proposes behind-the-curb improvements (sidewalks, ADA ramps, landscape strips) within existing street ROW but no new roadway construction or street extensions.
findings.reasoning: The condition is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. New roadway construction would involve creating new streets, not present on existing plans, requiring horizontal alignment, vertical profile, cross-sections, and pavement design. This project improves existing street frontages with sidewalks and landscape work but does not construct new roadways. The absence of roadway plan/profile sheets, absence of search results for roadway construction terms, and the infill nature of the development on established street network confirm no new roadway construction is proposed. Therefore, the condition is not met and this item is not applicable.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed; project involves improvements to existing streets only

findings.observation: Same analysis as CC-23-05. Searched for new roadway construction indicators and found none. The project does not propose new roadway construction. findings.reasoning: The condition is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. Target speed is a design parameter required for new roadway construction, governing geometric design, sight distance, and signage/striping. findings.observation: Condition check: 'If new roadway construction or work in ROW'. No new roadway construction (see CC-23-05), but there IS work in ROW — sheets 21 and 22 show extensive proposed behind-the-curb improvements including sidewalks, ADA ramps, curbing, landscape strips, and street trees within the right-of-way. Therefore the condition is met and this item applies. Examined sheet 13 titled 'OVERALL SITE & PAVING & STRIPING PLAN' via vision tool. The sheet shows paving types (concrete types, fire lanes) and building footprints. The legend includes a 'PROPOSED FIRE LANE' line type visible on the plan. However, the sheet does not show painted striping patterns (centerlines, edge lines, crosswalks, stop bars) in the street areas (South Lamar, Collier, Evergreen). No pavement markings are depicted within the ROW. No signage locations or types are indicated anywhere on the sheet — no symbols or callouts for stop signs, yield signs, ADA parking signs, or other traffic control devices.
findings.reasoning: The deficiency text requires a signage and striping plan for new or modified roadway in ROW. The condition 'new roadway construction or work in ROW' is met because there is work in ROW (sidewalks, curbs, ramps). When ROW work is performed, particularly work that modifies the streetscape and creates new pedestrian crossings (ADA ramps), a signage and striping plan is required to show pavement markings (crosswalks, stop bars) and traffic control signage. Sheet 13 is titled as a striping plan but does not show striping in the ROW — it shows internal site paving and fire lanes only. The absence of crosswalk markings at ADA ramp locations, absence of any pavement striping in the streets, and absence of any signage callouts constitutes a missing required plan element.
findings.explanation: Work in ROW is proposed (sidewalks, ADA ramps) but sheet 13 'Paving & Striping Plan' shows no striping or signage in ROW areas
findings.resolution: Provide signage and striping plan for right-of-way improvements. Show pavement markings including crosswalks at ADA ramp locations, stop bars, and any other required striping. Indicate signage locations and types for traffic control as needed for the ROW work.

The site plan set shows extensive ROW work (sidewalks, ADA ramps, curbing, landscape strips) that is systematically identified through multiple methods: (1) 'PROPOSED VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT' labels on sheets 14 and 21 explicitly name and delineate the ROW work area; (2) sidewalk spot elevations marked with 'SW' prefix throughout sheet 22 identify sidewalk construction in ROW; (3) key notes and ADA symbols identify ADA ramps in ROW; (4) dimension labels identify planting zones and clear zones in ROW. This multi-layered labeling approach provides clear identification that work is occurring in the ROW and describes the nature of that work.
